cohort: The study included 63,844 singleton live-born infants from the most recent birth of a mother within a 5-year period before each of three Nigeria Demographic and Health Surveys (2003, 2008, and 2013).
finding: Lack of formal maternal education, living in rural areas, and belonging to poor households were significantly associated with increased risk of postneonatal, infant, child, and under-5 mortality.
